test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which sector(s) employed the largest share of the working population in India on the eve of independence?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On the eve of India’s independence in **1947**, the **primary sector** was the largest employer of the Indian workforce. This sector includes agriculture, forestry, fishing, and other allied activities.
 
• The Indian economy was largely **agrarian** during British rule, with over 70% of the population dependent on agriculture for their livelihood.
 
• The economy was predominantly rural, with limited industrialization and negligible development in the **secondary** (manufacturing) and **tertiary** (services) sectors.
 
• The **primary sector** accounted for a substantial share of the national income, but it was characterized by low productivity, outdated technology, and a lack of investment.
 
• The exploitation of Indian agriculture under British colonial policies, such as the **zamindari system** and high land revenue demands, further contributed to the dominance of the primary sector in terms of employment, as most of the population relied on subsistence farming.
 
• The **secondary sector** (industrial sector) was underdeveloped during colonial rule as the British policies discouraged the growth of Indian industries to ensure dependence on British manufactured goods.
 
• The **tertiary sector**, which includes services like trade, transport, and banking, was also underdeveloped and catered primarily to the needs of colonial administration and foreign trade.
 
• Thus, the majority of the Indian population at the time of independence was employed in the **primary sector**, and the economy was heavily dependent on agriculture. *Hence, the correct answer is Primary sector.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Primary Sector:**

 
 
• The primary sector involves activities that are directly dependent on natural resources, such as **agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining**.
 
• In India, before independence, a significant majority of the population was engaged in agriculture and allied activities as their primary source of livelihood.
 
• The primary sector contributed the most to India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) during colonial rule, but it was marked by a lack of modernization and low productivity.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector:**
 
 
• The secondary sector includes industries that produce finished goods from raw materials, such as **manufacturing, construction, and industrial production**.
 
• During British rule, the secondary sector was underdeveloped as the colonial powers prioritized raw material extraction from India for industries in Britain, while deliberately restricting the growth of Indian industries.
 
• Examples include the decline of the Indian textile industry due to competition from British imports and the lack of capital investment in industrialization.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector:**
 
 
• The tertiary sector includes services like **trade, transport, banking, communication, and administration**.
 
• During colonial rule, the tertiary sector primarily served the needs of the British administration and foreign trade, with limited contribution to the general population’s employment.
 
• It was small in size compared to the primary sector and did not play a significant role in providing employment.
 
 
 
• **Post-Independence Developments:**
 
 
• After independence, efforts were made to diversify the economy by promoting industrialization and developing the secondary and tertiary sectors.
 
• Policies like the **Five-Year Plans**, establishment of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), and Green Revolution significantly contributed to reducing the over-reliance on agriculture.
 
• In recent years, the tertiary sector has emerged as the largest contributor to GDP, while the share of the primary sector has declined.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Agrarian Economy:** India’s economy during colonial rule was predominantly agrarian, with a majority of the population engaged in agriculture and related activities.
 
• **Exploitation of Indian Agriculture:** The British implemented exploitative systems like the **zamindari system**, which led to widespread poverty and low agricultural productivity.
 
• **Limited Industrialization:** The British policies hindered the development of industries in India, restricting employment opportunities in the secondary sector.
 
• **Economic Transition:** Post-independence, India witnessed a shift from an agrarian economy to a more diversified one, with significant growth in industrial and service sectors.
 
• **Current Scenario:** As of recent times, the **tertiary sector** has become the largest contributor to India’s GDP, while the primary sector employs a lower percentage of the population compared to the past.
